narrative.overview:
The portfolio behaves like a living GitHub profile: personal identity sits beside a readable project record, and repository conventions make the student's work feel inspectable rather than advertised. The interface is compact, factual, and familiar, with Primer semantics supplying the core visual language while the green monogram, progress marks, and profile composition keep the site personal.

The system is intentionally border-led and content-first. Muted canvases separate file headers, project metadata, and secondary states; links and status colors carry meaning rather than decoration. Light and dark themes remain equivalent expressions of the same semantic roles, and the persistent non-affiliation statement keeps the GitHub-inspired presentation honest.
keyCharacteristics: GitHub profile and README composition instead of a marketing hero.
Semantic Primer colors that remain meaningful across light and dark themes.
Repository borders, muted file surfaces, compact controls, and readable metadata.
Personal green identity accents reserved for primary action and progress.
Explicit presentation as an independent portfolio, not a GitHub property.

rules.name: The Semantic Token Rule
rules.body: Use Primer semantic custom properties for foregrounds, canvases, links, focus, and borders so light and dark themes change roles rather than individual selectors.

rules.name: The Green Reserve Rule
rules.body: Green is for personal identity, primary action, completion, and contribution-style progress; it is not a general decorative fill.

rules.name: The Independent Profile Rule
rules.body: GitHub colors and patterns describe the portfolio's hosting and interaction language, never endorsement, ownership, or official affiliation.

rules.name: The Repository Voice Rule
rules.body: Use the system sans stack at every level; hierarchy comes from restrained scale and weight, not from a contrasting display typeface.

rules.name: The Short Display Rule
rules.body: Large, tightly tracked headings stay brief and cap their line length at roughly 16–18 characters.

rules.name: The Profile-to-Record Rule
rules.body: On the overview, establish the person first and place the README-style work record directly beside them whenever the viewport allows.

rules.name: The Collapse, Don't Compress Rule
rules.body: When a rail or two-column composition no longer fits, stack it; do not preserve desktop columns by shrinking readable content.

rules.name: The Shared Edge Rule
rules.body: Repository groups use joined borders and aligned edges before separate card silhouettes.

rules.name: The Border-First Rule
rules.body: Establish hierarchy with borders and tonal surfaces before considering shadow.

rules.name: The Flat Record Rule
rules.body: README panels, project records, link rows, and repository cards remain visually attached to the page rather than hovering above it.

rules.name: The Primer Radius Rule
rules.body: Use the 6px control radius for buttons, mobile navigation items, and independent bounded panels.

rules.name: The Semantic Circle Rule
rules.body: Circular geometry signals identity, status, or a data point—not generic decoration.

dos: Do use semantic Primer foreground, background, border, link, and focus roles so both shipped themes remain coherent.
Do present projects like inspectable repository records: name, concise purpose, status, technology, and learning context.
Do use green sparingly for identity, primary action, completion, and contribution-style progress.
Do keep the profile/README relationship recognizable on wide screens and stack it cleanly on small screens.
Do retain the visible statement that the personal portfolio is not affiliated with GitHub.
Do preserve visible focus, semantic landmarks, reduced-motion behavior, and readable line lengths.
donts: Don't turn the site into a generic marketing landing page with oversized promotional chrome.
Don't hard-code theme-specific body colors where a Primer semantic custom property already expresses the role.
Don't scatter green across decorative surfaces or allow multiple primary actions to compete in one group.
Don't add routine shadows to repository cards, README panels, sidebars, or contact rows.
Don't imply that GitHub owns, endorses, or operates the portfolio.
Don't compress desktop rails into narrow unreadable columns; stack them at the established breakpoint.
